sections.name: model
sections.title: Model
sections.description: Provider, model and reasoning effort for new conversations. Existing sessions keep their model; /model saved adopts the default here.

sections.name: providers
sections.title: Wire protocol
sections.description: How direct provider connections are made: API surface and cache TTL.

sections.name: openrouter
sections.title: OpenRouter routing
sections.description: How OpenRouter picks a host; unset = sticky routing.

sections.name: failover
sections.title: Failover and retry
sections.description: What happens when a provider call fails or a quota runs out.

sections.name: appearance
sections.title: Appearance
sections.description: Theme and the terminal features the TUI is allowed to use.

sections.name: keymap
sections.title: Hotkeys
sections.description: Keys for starting and resuming conversations. Press enter on a row, then press the key you want.

sections.name: approvals
sections.title: Approvals
sections.description: Whether write and command tools prompt, in every running session. A config write tightens every running session at once; loosening one needs a write from that session's own process (/approvals auto in it, or a /settings page in that process).

sections.name: session
sections.title: Session storage
sections.description: Autosave. The cleanup policies have their own sections below.

sections.name: session_cleanup
sections.title: Your conversations
sections.description: Session cleanup for the conversations you started and the workstreams in your sidebar. Off by default; nothing here runs until you switch it on.

sections.name: session_delegated
sections.title: Delegated work
sections.description: Delegated work: subagent and background-session transcripts and their scratch folders. On by default: they are removed after the age below. Your conversations, sidebar workstreams, anything running, waiting on a wake or monitor, linked to an open project, still in use by an active parent, or holding unpushed or uncommitted git work are kept.

sections.name: subagents
sections.title: Subagents
sections.description: Concurrency cap, child knowledge slimming, who picks a child's model, and the model each tier runs on.

sections.name: classification
sections.title: Smart hints
sections.description: Advisory skills, guides and MCP servers a decision model may suggest per message. Off keeps the prompt unchanged.

sections.name: supplements
sections.title: Highlights
sections.description: After an answer, point out the files it produced and, when you turn it on, draw a chart of numbers it showed. Off by environment: LOP_SUPPLEMENTS=0.

sections.name: monitor
sections.title: Monitors
sections.description: Delta-watching monitors: how often they check, how much they keep, and when they give up.

sections.name: runtime
sections.title: Runtime
sections.description: How sessions behave when you leave them. The warm-runtime knobs are read when a runtime next draws its window.

sections.name: compaction
sections.title: Compaction
sections.description: When the conversation is summarised to reclaim context.

sections.name: fork
sections.title: Fork
sections.description: Where /fork opens the branched conversation.

sections.name: web_tools
sections.title: Web tools
sections.description: Whether the search and fetch tools are offered and allowed to run.

sections.name: web_search
sections.title: Web search
sections.description: Providers and load balancing for the search tool.

sections.name: web_fetch
sections.title: Web fetch
sections.description: Limits and rendering for the fetch tool.

sections.name: tools
sections.title: Tools
sections.description: How the built-in tools execute.

sections.name: hooks
sections.title: Hooks
sections.description: Run native and forwarded Claude Code / Codex PostToolUse hooks.

sections.name: memory_guard
sections.title: Command memory limit
sections.description: A per-command RAM ceiling, so one oversized command is killed instead of taking the whole device down.

sections.name: query_budget
sections.title: Shell query budget
sections.description: Time budget for a shell query — a grep/find/du walk rather than a build or an install: an advisory at 10 s, and a stop at the budget so one search cannot spend minutes of a turn.

sections.name: shell_environment
sections.title: Agent shell
sections.description: What a command the agent runs can see. Resolved once per session, so an edit here applies at the next launch and cannot weaken a session that is already running.

sections.name: local_providers
sections.title: Local servers
sections.description: Server endpoints and exact-model metadata. Use /login to connect; reselect with /model saved to apply model changes.

sections.name: console
sections.title: Console capacity
sections.description: Live terminal admission. Completed history does not consume process slots. Changes affect future starts, never terminate running work.

sections.name: desktop
sections.title: Desktop app
sections.description: Where a notification click sends you when the desktop app is not running.

sections.name: static
sections.title: File previews
sections.description: Extra directories the local server may serve image, audio, video and HTML previews from. The agent home, session folders, uploads and the working directories of your agents and running sessions are always included.

sections.name: network
sections.title: Mesh network
sections.description: Where this device listens, what it tells peers to dial, and the bounds for `lop network`: audit retention, how many unauthenticated connections the relay will hold at once, session-copy cadence and how long a borrowed login lives. All take effect when the relay restarts.

sections.name: mesh_updates
sections.title: Mesh updates
sections.description: The roll that follows a local update: after `lop update` moves this device to a newer build, every other active member is asked to move to the same build — one at a time, each waiting for that member to go idle, never forced. A member that has not granted this device `update` is skipped, by name, with the remedy. Takes effect at once: the next update uses the new setting, and a roll already running stops before its next member — an install already begun finishes.

sections.name: aida
sections.title: Aida
sections.description: Your chief of staff: her display name, and the proactive cadence — when she checks in, how much she may escalate, and the pause switch. The name applies everywhere at once; edits are read at her next action, and /aida pause|resume act immediately.

sections.name: hub
sections.title: Agent Hub
sections.description: Keep agents and teams you pulled from the Agent Hub current: whether updates are merged in automatically, how often the hub is checked, and which model resolves a conflict. Your edits and deletions are merged, never overwritten.

sections.name: agents
sections.title: Agents
sections.description: Whether installed starter roles (reviewer, coder, aida, ...) update themselves to the packaged text at launch when you have not edited them. Off = updates are still reported; apply them with 'lop agents sync'.

sections.name: projects
sections.title: Projects
sections.description: Project records: how long a tracked project may go without a progress line before it reads stale and is worth a check-in. Read at the next staleness computation.

sections.name: wakes
sections.title: Wake triggers
sections.description: When a watched condition goes stale, the assistant is woken to check in rather than left to wait for the daily cadence: the master switch, the per-day budget and spacing, and which sources may fire. Read at the next evaluation pass.

sections.name: proactive
sections.title: Proactive class
sections.description: Bounds for the proactive agent class: how long a hidden patience wait defaults to, how it backs off across re-attempts, and when a cycle must end. Read at the moment a wait is armed or fires.

sections.name: speech
sections.title: Speech voicing
sections.description: How the assistant sounds when it speaks aloud. The descriptor is sent to the hub, which maps it onto whichever voice provider serves; fields a provider cannot express degrade with a note rather than failing. Read on the next spoken message.

sections.name: team_bridge
sections.title: Agent messages
sections.description: Your agent can exchange messages with other members' agents in your organization. Off by default; you can pause or turn it off at any time.

sections.name: retired
sections.title: Retired
sections.description: Keys that are read but no longer do anything.

sections.name: memory
sections.title: Memory
sections.description: Bounded local recall and best-effort compaction capture; retrieved facts are untrusted.

sections.name: asks
sections.title: Asks
sections.description: Questions an agent queues for you. A change applies at once in the terminal, the desktop app and on your phone.

settings.label: Scoped memory
settings.help: Enable the bounded SQLite memory bank. Turning this off does not erase retained facts.

settings.label: Compaction capture
settings.help: Capture safe locators after committed compactions; context-full also reuses its existing summary. Explicit stores remain the guaranteed route for goals and decisions.

settings.label: Recall suggestions
settings.help: Suggest up to three untrusted titles from the current user message, within a separate 180-token cap. No network or embedding request.

settings.label: Trusted-peer memory sync
settings.help: Incrementally share selected scopes with existing paired receiver-admin peers supporting memory-sync-v1. This includes session memories without copying transcripts.

settings.label: Memory scopes to sync
settings.help: Only these namespaces are shared. Session, team and agent owners remain exact registry/session IDs; all four scopes are supported.

settings.label: Excluded memory peers
settings.help: Device IDs excluded from memory replication. This does not change pairing, trust or enrollment grants.

settings.label: Default provider
settings.help: Provider for new conversations. /model saved adopts it here.

settings.label: Default model
settings.help: Model for new conversations. /model saved adopts it here.

settings.label: Default reasoning effort
settings.help: Effort for new conversations. Unset: the model's default.

choices.label: minimal
choices.description: the least reasoning the model offers

settings.label: Use maximum OpenAI context
settings.help: Off: provider default. On: supported max. Applies next request; compaction unchanged.

settings.label: OpenAI API surface
settings.help: Direct OpenAI GPT-5 calls use the Responses API unless opted out.

settings.label: Anthropic 1h cache above (tokens)
settings.help: Context size from which Anthropic requests use the 1-hour prompt-cache TTL (2x write cost, survives idle gaps over 5 minutes). 0 disables.

settings.label: cache affinity
settings.help: Reuses the host that served the previous turn so the prompt cache stays warm. Off = OpenRouter's price-weighted load balancing.

settings.label: routing policy
settings.help: How OpenRouter ranks hosts for this call. May route away from the host holding your warm prompt cache (a cold start on long conversations); 'default' sends no preference at all.

choices.label: default
choices.description: no preference — sticky routing stays on (warmest cache)

settings.label: host order
settings.help: Empty = no opinion (sticky routing stays). Comma-separated host slugs tried in this exact order.
settings.warning: disables sticky routing — prompt cache goes cold

settings.label: allowed hosts
settings.help: Empty = no opinion (sticky routing stays). Comma-separated allow-list of host slugs; every other host is excluded — a forced cold start if the warm host is not on it.

settings.label: ignored hosts
settings.help: Empty = no opinion (sticky routing stays). Comma-separated block-list of host slugs to omit (e.g. a host that is failing right now) — may cost you the warm prompt cache.

settings.label: fallbacks
settings.help: 'default' sends nothing (OpenRouter falls through to another host when the preferred one fails); 'false' fails rather than fall through to a host outside your preferences.

settings.label: require parameters
settings.help: 'true' restricts to hosts that support every parameter you send (tools, structured output); 'default' lets OpenRouter silently drop unsupported ones.

choices.label: default
choices.description: no preference — unsupported parameters may be dropped

choices.label: true
choices.description: only hosts that support every parameter

settings.label: data collection
settings.help: 'deny' excludes hosts that may train on or retain your prompts. 'default' sends no preference (OpenRouter's default: allow).

settings.label: zero data retention
settings.help: 'true': restrict to zero-data-retention endpoints. 'default': nothing sent.

settings.label: distillable text
settings.help: 'true': restrict to endpoints whose text output may be distilled. 'default': nothing sent.

settings.label: quantizations
settings.help: Empty = no opinion. Comma-separated quantization levels the served model may use (e.g. int8, fp8, mxfp4).

settings.label: max price
settings.help: {"prompt": 1, "completion": 2} — USD / million tokens

settings.label: min throughput (tok/s)
settings.help: Prefer hosts serving at least this many output tokens/sec (p50). 0 sends no preference. A host below the bar is deprioritised, which may cost you a warm prompt cache.

settings.label: max latency (s)
settings.help: Prefer hosts whose time-to-first-token stays under this many seconds (p50). 0 sends no preference. A host above the bar is deprioritised, which may cost you a warm prompt cache.

settings.label: retire slow host (tok/s)
settings.help: Experimental, off by default: evidence is from one model/run. A positive floor stops pinning a host after three long replies below this output-token/sec rate, excluding local consumer time. 0 clears speed exclusions on the next request; cache-miss exclusions remain. Moving hosts may start a cold prompt cache.

settings.label: Retry failed calls
settings.help: Retry a failed provider call before surfacing the error.

settings.label: Max retries
settings.help: Fast budget against a reachable provider (5xx, timeout).

settings.label: Base delay (ms)
settings.help: First backoff step; later attempts grow from it.

settings.label: Connectivity retries
settings.help: Patient budget for a machine that went offline; distinct from max retries.

settings.label: Connectivity backoff cap (ms)
settings.help: Longest wait between connectivity retries.

settings.label: Model fallback
settings.help: Move to the next hop in the cascade when a model keeps failing.

choices.label: on
choices.description: fall back to the next hop

settings.label: Usage-aware fallback
settings.help: Switch before a quota runs out. Costs one quota request per user message.

settings.label: account selection policy
settings.help: Chooses eligible sibling accounts within the same provider and credential tier. A compatible, unexpired lease from a successful request takes priority for every policy; it does not guarantee a cache hit. Reset soonest prefers the nearest weekly refill, then the five-hour refill within one-minute ties. An explicit policy overrides the legacy usage-aware account pick setting.

choices.label: Reset soonest
choices.description: Prefer the nearest included-plan reset; spread ties and unknown reports deterministically. Default for new configurations.

choices.label: Most headroom
choices.description: Prefer cached remaining quota, spreading accounts within ten percentage points of the best.

choices.label: Fair spread
choices.description: Use a stable session-based spread instead of ranking cached resets or remaining quota.

settings.label: legacy usage-aware pick
settings.help: Compatibility setting, used only when account selection policy is absent: true selects Most headroom; false selects Fair spread. An explicit account selection policy takes precedence. Reset the account selection policy row to restore Reset soonest and clear legacy overrides.

settings.label: Usage reserve (%)
settings.help: Headroom below which an account counts as low; a running session stays on it.

settings.label: Failover cascade
settings.help: Ordered provider/model hops tried when a call keeps failing.

settings.label: Pinned child fallback
settings.help: What a pinned child may fall back to: same-family hops only, or any vendor (announced).

settings.label: Theme
settings.help: Colour ramp. /theme switches it live with an arrow-key preview.

settings.label: Shimmer animation
settings.help: The animated sheen on the working line.

settings.label: Mid-turn narration
settings.help: Keep the agent's mid-turn narration in the transcript after its tool calls run.

settings.label: Live model reasoning
settings.help: Show the model's private thinking while it streams; it vanishes once the thinking ends.

settings.label: Assistant gutter rail
settings.help: A rule marks the ANSWER: the message that ends the turn. Mid-turn narration takes no rail.

settings.label: Comfortable action rows
settings.help: Pad tool and prompt rows so they are easier to click.

settings.label: Nerd Font glyphs
settings.help: Expanded tool-row icons. Auto reads the terminal emulator's markers.

settings.label: Heading markers
settings.help: Show the literal ### before a heading, as the markdown source writes it.

settings.label: Terminal title
settings.help: OSC 0 window title carrying the session name and run state.

settings.label: Inline images
settings.help: Screenshots and attachments drawn in the transcript.

settings.label: Desktop notifications
settings.help: Fires only while the terminal is unfocused.

settings.label: Notification session names
settings.help: A session's name, last line and error causes appear on banners, including the lock screen.

settings.label: Wake time format
settings.help: Scheduled wake times use your local timezone. Choose a 12- or 24-hour clock.

settings.label: Language
settings.help: Interface language. auto follows your operating system, falling back to English.

settings.label: Subagent dock
settings.help: How much room the subagent panel takes when a session starts; ctrl+g cycles it.

choices.label: full
choices.description: one row per child, newest first

settings.label: Hide cross-session traffic
settings.help: Hide lop send traffic and inbound peer messages from transcripts.

settings.label: Mark the turn answer
settings.help: Draw a thin rule beside the answer that closes a turn (desktop app).

settings.label: Status band
settings.help: Also the standing alerts. Model, dir, context, cost, rate, elapsed.

settings.label: Prompt chevron
settings.help: The prompt mark at the left edge of the input row.

settings.label: Band: model
settings.help: The model-label segment in the status band.

settings.label: Band: working dir
settings.help: The working-directory segment in the status band.

settings.label: Band: context
settings.help: The context-usage segment in the status band.

settings.label: Band: decode rate
settings.help: The tok/s segment — the last completed call's throughput.

settings.label: Band: session cost
settings.help: The session-cost segment in the status band.

settings.label: Band: elapsed
settings.help: The elapsed-time segment in the status band.

settings.label: Session sidebar
settings.help: Active and recent conversations. Ctrl+B toggles the sidebar.

settings.label: Sidebar position
settings.help: Which side of the conversation holds the session sidebar.

choices.label: left
choices.description: sessions to the left of the conversation

choices.label: right
choices.description: sessions to the right of the conversation

settings.label: Sidebar subagent layer
settings.help: List recent subagent runs below your own sessions. Ctrl+A toggles the layer while the sidebar has focus.

settings.label: New session
settings.help: Starts a fresh conversation, the same as /new.

settings.label: Resume a session
settings.help: Opens the picker of recent conversations, the same as /resume.

settings.label: Quick send
settings.help: Opens a small composer over other apps; messages the chief of staff.

settings.label: Push to talk
settings.help: Hold to dictate (desktop); release to stop.

settings.label: Tool approval mode
settings.help: Loosening needs a write in this session — /approvals auto.

settings.label: Auto-save conversation
settings.help: Headless REPL launches only; the TUI's runtime does not read it.

settings.label: Keep working after /resume
settings.help: Leave a running turn working when you switch away from its session.

choices.label: on

choices.label: off
choices.description: stop the turn when you leave the session

settings.label: Keep closed conversations warm (s)
settings.help: Re-opening inside this window attaches to the live runtime. 0 keeps nothing warm.

settings.label: Max warm conversations
settings.help: Cap on warm runtimes in this install; the least recently closed exits first.

settings.label: Session cleanup
settings.help: Off: nothing is ever removed. On: limits below run at launch, sparing the newest 10 + live.

choices.label: on

settings.label: ↳ max sessions

settings.label: ↳ max inactive days
settings.help: Needs cleanup on. Remove sessions idle this many days; 0 = never.

settings.label: ↳ max total bytes
settings.help: Needs cleanup on. Trim oldest past this many bytes; 0 = no cap.

settings.label: ↳ remove empty
settings.help: Needs cleanup on. Remove dirs that never got a transcript.

settings.label: Delegated cleanup
settings.help: Remove subagent and background-session transcripts after the age below; never your conversations or anything in use.

choices.label: on
choices.description: remove delegated work after the age below

settings.label: ↳ remove after (hours)
settings.help: Hours idle before removal: 2 to 720 (30 days). Default 48.

settings.label: Unattended question timeout (h)
settings.help: How long a question waits when you are away. 0 never times out.

settings.label: Max background jobs

settings.label: Max nested-team depth

settings.help: Needs Highlights on. Draw a chart when an answer shows numbers. Spends model tokens.

choices.label: on
choices.description: a chart may be generated (spends tokens)

settings.label: ↳ graphics model
settings.help: Needs graphics on. auto picks a cheap fast model; session uses this session's.

settings.label: ↳ max turns
settings.help: Needs graphics on. Model turns per chart, including one repair.

settings.label: ↳ max output tokens
settings.help: Needs graphics on. Output budget per generator turn.

settings.label: ↳ time limit (s)
settings.help: Needs Highlights on. Give up on a whole job after this long.

settings.label: ↳ cost cap ($)
settings.help: Needs graphics on. Soft cap on one job's spend.

settings.label: ↳ files shown
settings.help: Needs Highlights on. Files named before the rest fold into 'N more'.

settings.label: ↳ never list under
settings.help: Needs Highlights on. Comma-separated folders whose files are never listed or sent to a decision model; use it on a machine holding customer data.

settings.label: Where a fork opens
settings.help: Choose where the fork opens; unfinished work stays in the original.

choices.label: new window
choices.description: open the fork elsewhere; this session keeps running

choices.label: this terminal
choices.description: follow the fork here; return with /resume

settings.label: Where it opens under cmux
settings.help: Under cmux, whether a fork gets its own workspace or a surface here.

choices.label: new workspace
choices.description: a sidebar row of its own

choices.label: new surface
choices.description: a tab in the current workspace

settings.label: Compaction
settings.help: Summarise older history when the context fills.

settings.label: Strategy
settings.help: Which mechanism compacts. Auto picks per model.

choices.label: auto
choices.description: snapcompact for vision models, else context-full

settings.label: Threshold (% of window)
settings.help: Percentage trigger. 0.80 and 80 both mean 80%.

settings.label: Threshold (tokens)
settings.help: Absolute trigger. The smaller of this and the percentage wins.

settings.label: Keep recent tokens
settings.help: Recent history kept verbatim across a pass.

settings.label: Continue after compaction
settings.help: Schedule a continuation prompt after a successful post-turn pass.

settings.label: Mid-turn compaction
settings.help: Allow a pass at safe tool-loop boundaries, not only between turns.

settings.label: Request size limit (bytes)
settings.help: Hard ceiling on the request. Older screenshots are dropped from the context (never from the transcript) to stay under it. 0 disables.

settings.label: Request size trigger (bytes)
settings.help: Compact once the request passes this size, so a screenshot-heavy session summarises early instead of dropping frames. 0 disables.

settings.label: Web search
settings.help: Offer the search tool and let it run; off refuses every call.

settings.label: Load balancing
settings.help: How the provider list is consumed.

choices.label: ordered
choices.description: top of the list first, fall through

settings.label: Providers
settings.help: Comma-separated, in priority order; tried before the automatic free providers.

settings.label: Excluded providers
settings.help: Never used, even in the automatic chain. Comma-separated; empty = none excluded.

settings.label: Timeout (s)
settings.help: Per-provider request timeout. Clamped to 1-120 when read.

settings.label: SearXNG endpoint
settings.help: Base URL of a self-hosted SearXNG instance.

settings.label: DeepSeek page evidence
settings.help: Adds a per-page quote and relevance score after a DeepSeek search.

settings.label: Read from search
settings.help: Offer web_read: answer from pages a search already retrieved, no refetch.

settings.label: Web fetch
settings.help: Offer the fetch tool and read <url>; off refuses every call.

settings.label: Timeout (s)
settings.help: Per-request timeout.

settings.label: Download ceiling (bytes)
settings.help: Enforced during streaming, so a huge page is cut off rather than buffered.

settings.label: Max redirects
settings.help: Redirect hops followed before giving up.

settings.label: Cache TTL (s)
settings.help: 0 disables the URL cache entirely.

settings.label: Allow private addresses
settings.help: SSRF guard. On permits loopback, private and link-local targets.

settings.label: HTML renderer
settings.help: Auto uses markdownify when the [fetch] extra is installed.

settings.label: Enrich before scraping
settings.help: Try .md, llms.txt and content negotiation before scraping HTML.

settings.label: Attempts per hop
settings.help: Retries share the call's timeout, so more attempts never take longer.

settings.label: Browser-profile retry
settings.help: After a refusal, retry once with browser-shaped headers.

settings.label: Native hooks
settings.help: Run hooks from hooks.json in the lop config dir after each tool call.

settings.label: Forward Claude Code hooks
settings.help: Run PostToolUse hooks from ~/.claude and plugins after each tool call.

settings.label: Forward Codex hooks
settings.help: Run PostToolUse hooks from ~/.codex/hooks.json after each tool call.

settings.label: Bash interpreter
settings.help: Interpreter for the bash tool. Empty uses bash on PATH, else /bin/sh.

settings.label: Journal unacknowledged sends
settings.help: Write a transcript notice when a `send` is not acknowledged. The tool result always reports it; this keeps a durable row too.

settings.label: Block unbounded searches
settings.help: Refuse a shell `grep`/`rg`/`find` that recurses from a repository root or a vendor/build tree, and point the agent at the `grep` tool. A scoped or single-file search is never touched. Off disables the check.

settings.label: ...refuse rather than warn
settings.help: On: the command is refused with a suggestion. Off: it runs anyway and the interception is logged, so an operator can watch before enforcing.

settings.label: ...prune vendor trees for ripgrep
settings.help: Give ripgrep a generated config that skips node_modules/.git/out etc., so an `rg` the guard does not block is still fast. Applies to ripgrep only.

settings.label: Load rarely used tool schemas on demand
settings.help: Keep rarely used tools' schemas out of every request until the agent reads tool://<name> or calls one. The tools stay callable either way. Off sends every schema on every request.

settings.label: Command memory limit
settings.help: Give every bash command a RAM ceiling. A command whose process group crosses it is killed (its group only, never lop) so it cannot take the device down; the model is told to use less memory.

settings.label: Ceiling source
settings.help: 'auto' derives the ceiling from the memory this device has free right now, so it tightens on its own when the machine is busy. 'manual' pins it to the number below.

settings.label: Manual ceiling (MB)
settings.help: The ceiling when 'manual' is selected above. 0 means use the auto ceiling instead, so leaving this at 0 never disables the guard.

settings.label: Advisory threshold
settings.help: Fraction of the ceiling at which one advisory line is emitted. It is only an advisory — userspace cannot slow an allocation — so it warns before the kill, it does not prevent it.

settings.label: Shell query budget
settings.help: Time-box a shell `grep`/`find`/`du` walk that reads the filesystem rather than a scoped file: one advisory at 10 s, then a stop at the budget below. Builds, installs and test runs are never affected.

settings.label: ...stop rather than warn
settings.help: On: a query that crosses the budget is killed and told why. Off: it runs to completion and only the advisory is shown, so an operator can watch before enforcing.

settings.label: Budget (seconds)
settings.help: Wall-clock budget for one shell query. The advisory fires at 10 s whatever this says; this is the stop. A per-command prefix of LOCAL_OPERATOR_ALLOW_SLOW_QUERY=1 skips the stop for a justified run.

settings.label: Agent shell environment
settings.help: 'inherit' lets a command the agent runs see your environment (gh, aws, npm keep their tokens). 'allowlist' passes only PATH/HOME/SHELL/TERM/USER/LOGNAME plus the two lists beside this, so the provider key this session launched with is not handed to a command the model writes. Read once per session: changing it takes effect at the next launch.

choices.label: allowlist
choices.description: the safe set plus the lists below, nothing else

settings.label: …kept in allowlist mode
settings.help: Empty = the safe set alone. Names the allowlist mode keeps ON TOP of the safe set — e.g. LOCAL_OPERATOR_CONFIG_DIR for a shell that must still resolve $(lop secret get NAME), or LANG. Inert in inherit mode.

settings.label: …removed in both modes
settings.help: Empty = nothing removed. Names never handed to a command the agent runs, in either mode — including the session credential store's own injections, so this is how a variable is denied outright. Covers the bash and eval children only; MCP servers and the harness's own processes are not governed by it.

settings.label: LM Studio endpoint
settings.help: HTTP(S) API root. Changing servers requires a new token through /login; existing tokens are never forwarded to another endpoint.

settings.label: LM Studio model overrides
settings.help: JSON: {"model-id":{"context_window":8192}}; server limits still apply.

settings.label: Ollama endpoint
settings.help: HTTP(S) API root. Changing servers requires a new token through /login; existing tokens are never forwarded to another endpoint.

settings.label: Ollama model overrides
settings.help: JSON: {"model-id":{"context_window":8192}}; server limits still apply.

settings.label: vLLM endpoint
settings.help: HTTP(S) API root. Changing servers requires a new token through /login; existing tokens are never forwarded to another endpoint.

settings.label: vLLM model overrides
settings.help: JSON: {"model-id":{"context_window":8192}}; server limits still apply.

settings.label: llama.cpp endpoint
settings.help: HTTP(S) API root. Changing servers requires a new token through /login; existing tokens are never forwarded to another endpoint.

settings.label: llama.cpp model overrides
settings.help: JSON: {"model-id":{"context_window":8192}}; server limits still apply.

settings.label: OpenAI-compatible endpoint
settings.help: HTTP(S) API root. Changing servers requires a new token through /login; existing tokens are never forwarded to another endpoint.

settings.label: OpenAI-compatible model overrides
settings.help: JSON: {"model-id":{"context_window":8192}}; server limits still apply.

settings.label: Conversation length
settings.help: Deprecated. Superseded by the compaction engine.

settings.label: Detail length
settings.help: Deprecated. Superseded by the compaction engine.

settings.label: Max learnings history
settings.help: Deprecated. Superseded by the compaction engine.

settings.label: Smart hints notice
settings.help: Deprecated. Smart hints is silent in the chat; the call is in the log.

settings.label: Live terminal ceiling
settings.help: 32–256; default 128. Managed memory, terminal cells and available native resources can admit fewer terminals. This does not limit child-process memory.

settings.label: Agent terminals per conversation
settings.help: 1–32; default 8. Each conversation shares the global live allowance; completed terminals do not count.

settings.label: Slots reserved for user terminals
settings.help: 4–32; default 16, capped at one quarter of the live ceiling. Agent starts cannot consume these slots. Existing work is never stopped.

settings.label: launch command
settings.help: Empty = discover the app (local-operator-ui, then the macOS app). {session} is the session id.

settings.label: Extra preview roots
settings.help: Empty = only the built-in roots. Consulted only by the fallback posture (a connection that is not loopback): normal loopback previews can serve any readable file. Comma-separated absolute directories; dot-directories below a root are never served.
settings.warning: only applies to the fallback (non-loopback) posture

settings.label: Listen address
settings.help: 127.0.0.1 = dial-only; 0.0.0.0 = all; or one address.

settings.label: Mesh port
settings.help: The port peers dial; endpoints without one use it.

settings.label: Advertised endpoints
settings.help: Empty = detected. Others: host:port, e.g. 203.0.113.7:4097

settings.label: Audit size per generation
settings.help: Bytes per generation, after rotation. 8 MiB of gzipped JSONL is roughly 55k records; the five-generation ceiling is therefore ~40 MiB.

settings.label: Audit generations kept
settings.help: Rotated files kept before the oldest is pruned and that pruning is recorded.

settings.label: Audit age cap (days)
settings.help: Age and size both rotate, because age binds on a quiet install and size on a busy one. Export with `lop network log --export` before pruning.

settings.label: Roll the mesh after an update
settings.help: After `lop update` installs a newer build here, ask this device's mesh members to move to it: one at a time, each waiting for idle, never forced. Off: only `lop network update` rolls. A member that has not granted this device `update` is skipped, with the remedy to grant it there.

choices.label: auto
choices.description: roll when an update moves to a newer build

settings.label: Concurrent handshakes
settings.help: Unauthenticated connections this relay will hold at once. A pairing holds one for the seconds until the code is typed; anything past the cap is dropped at accept, with no reply frame.

settings.label: Sync quiet period (s)
settings.help: Seconds a session's transcript must stay unchanged before its owner tells devices holding a copy to pull. A session going idle pushes at once, so its final message is never held back by this.

settings.label: Sync check interval (s)
settings.help: How often the owner checks copied sessions for changes: one file stat each.

settings.label: Borrowed login lifetime (s)
settings.help: The longest a device may use a login it borrowed from its owner before asking again, and so how long a revoked or offline owner's login keeps working elsewhere. Never longer than the token itself.

settings.label: GitHub repositories
settings.help: owner/repo entries a brokered GitHub token may touch (empty: none)

settings.label: Auto-update agents
settings.help: Merge hub updates into pulled agents automatically.

choices.label: off
choices.description: only tell me; I apply them

settings.label: Auto-update teams
settings.help: Merge hub updates into pulled teams automatically.

choices.label: off
choices.description: only tell me; I apply them

settings.label: Check interval (minutes)
settings.help: Minutes between hub update checks (both modes).

settings.label: Auto-update built-in roles
settings.help: At launch, update unedited built-ins; tool changes still ask.

choices.label: off
choices.description: only tell me; I apply them

settings.label: Chief of staff enabled
settings.help: Read at boot and by /aida; a disabled install never creates her session.

settings.label: Display name
settings.help: What she is called everywhere. Renaming her conversation or /aida rename <name> updates it.

settings.label: Daily check-in time
settings.help: Local wall-clock HH:MM. An invalid value falls back to 08:30 at the next arm.

settings.label: Check-in interval (hours)
settings.help: 0 keeps the daily local check-in time. 1–168 uses elapsed hours; 4 checks in every four hours. Changes preserve an already-owed check-in.

settings.label: Cadence paused
settings.help: Written by /aida pause|resume, which also hold her wakes; editing it here works the same way at her next tick.

settings.label: Extra check-ins / day
settings.help: How many escalation check-ins she may arm per day. 0 disables escalation.

settings.label: Minimum gap (minutes)
settings.help: Minimum spacing between her wakes; closer requests are refused.

settings.label: Integration nudge interval (days)
settings.help: How rarely she may nudge about setting up an integration. Read from the onboarding slice.

settings.label: Stale after (hours)
settings.help: A project whose progress is older than this reads stale and is worth a check-in. 1–168 hours.

settings.label: Enabled
settings.help: Master switch for trigger wakes; off means no check-in is ever created.

settings.label: Max check-in wakes per day
settings.help: Per-target rolling 24 h budget for trigger wakes. 0 disables trigger wakes without touching the switch above.

settings.label: Minimum gap (minutes)
settings.help: Minimum spacing between trigger wakes to the same target.

settings.label: Project staleness trigger
settings.help: Wake to check in on projects whose progress went stale. Settled (done/paused/archived) projects are never watched.

settings.label: Default patience wait (ms)
settings.help: How long a hidden wait defaults to when the agent does not size one (milliseconds; 300000 = 5 min). Clamped 60 s..24 h.

settings.label: Patience backoff factor
settings.help: Each later wait in a cycle is at least this many times the first — the default 5/15/45-minute progression.

settings.label: Patience max attempts
settings.help: How many outbound waits one cycle may hold before it must end.

settings.label: Patience cycle TTL (ms)
settings.help: Hard stop for one cycle however the waits were sized (milliseconds; 7200000 = 2 h). A fire past it retires silently.

settings.label: Pending waits per session
settings.help: How many hidden waits may be pending at once for one session.

settings.label: Voice gender
settings.help: auto picks per agent; a fixed value overrides the classifier.

settings.label: Tone
settings.help: Warmth of delivery. Honoured as a voice row or emulated in instructions.

settings.label: Expressiveness
settings.help: How animated the delivery is. Sets ElevenLabs stability; a phrase on OpenAI.

settings.label: Pace
settings.help: Speaking rate, 1.0 being normal. A provider whose own range is narrower clamps.

settings.label: Language
settings.help: auto lets the provider detect; a two-letter code (e.g. es) pins it.

settings.label: Accent
settings.help: A region tag such as en-GB, or empty. Reaches the provider as instructions text.

settings.label: Delivery instructions
settings.help: Free text for how speech should sound (OpenAI only). Empty sends none of our own.
settings.value: Speak aloud and pay attention to potentially multilingual inputs and make sure to use native accents for all different parts of the text, especially those that are not english. Strive for a casual and native-sounding conversational tone. Don't over-enunciate, consider word combinations that should have silent and natural transitions, like "raha hoon" -> "rahoon" or "je m'appelle" -> "jm'appelle".
settings.default: Speak aloud and pay attention to potentially multilingual inputs and make sure to use native accents for all different parts of the text, especially those that are not english. Strive for a casual and native-sounding conversational tone. Don't over-enunciate, consider word combinations that should have silent and natural transitions, like "raha hoon" -> "rahoon" or "je m'appelle" -> "jm'appelle".

settings.label: Enabled on this machine
settings.help: Off by default. Also needs a Radient sign-in and an eligible organization.

settings.label: CoS session
settings.help: Session that may be woken for new messages; empty = badge only.

settings.label: Show timed-out asks for
settings.help: How long an unanswered ask stays shown past its deadline.

choices.label: gone at expiry
choices.description: hidden as soon as it times out
